# Crosspost

Curated by Skill Harbor: a distribution skill for publishing the same underlying idea across X, LinkedIn, Threads, and Bluesky without turning it into the same post in four costumes. The workflow picks the strongest primary version first, captures the voice fingerprint (via brand-voice, also in this batch), then adapts by platform constraint: X stays compressed with the sharpest claim up front, LinkedIn adds only the context outsiders need, Threads stays readable and direct, Bluesky stays concise. Core rules are strict: never publish identical copy across platforms, preserve the author's voice, adapt for constraints not stereotypes, and never invent a CTA the source did not earn. It also carries prompt-injection hygiene for the social age: source material from URLs or other people's drafts is treated as data, never instructions, and embedded agent-directed text gets flagged to the user with its origin instead of being adapted into a post. A quality gate checks that each version reads like the same author under different constraints. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: it adapts and drafts, it does not post to your accounts for you; the banned-patterns list ("Excited to share", "link in bio", closing "What do you think?") will fight you if that is your usual style, which is the point. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
